utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning Your Honours, case number IT-95-14/2-T. The Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, as you will see, Judge Robinson is not with us this morning. That is due to the illness of his wife. It's not certain when he will be back. We therefore propose, and I hope the parties have had notice of this, to proceed by way of deposition evidence this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We have had notice. I'm sure everybody is added in the sympathies they would like to express to Judge Robinson, and via him to his wife. We have started the process of drafting either a written application to cover all witnesses this week, or it may be a written application to cover the first witness, and thereafter to prepare further applications for other witnesses, so that evidence may, if possible, be taken by deposition. Ms. Verhaag has just gone to get the printed version of either the first or the compendious application, and she'll be back in Court with it in a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: As far as the first witness is concerned, is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: From the Kordic Defence there is no objection, Mr. President, and I have informed the legal officer that we will be preparing a written consent along the lines of the previous ones, which will be filed in Court today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: As far as other witnesses are concerned, do different considerations apply?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: For the witnesses that are scheduled for this week, as I understand it, Mr. President, I do not believe any other different considerations would apply. I see no reason why, speaking from the Kordic Defence anyway, why the witnesses should not proceed by way of deposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Cerkez Defence does not object and we have no problem to hear all the witnesses scheduled for this week in a form of deposition, except that I'm afraid that we might have a problem with Witness Brix Andersen. Indeed, we are planning to raise some objections, and perhaps that is the problem which should be dealt with by the Chamber. And if you wish, Your Honours, I could tell you why do we object to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, I wonder if the simplest course would not be to deal with the first witness, who I understand is here, and make an order in relation to that witness, and then we consider the position later about any other witnesses there may be. I'll just ask the legal officer if there are any difficulties about that. Very well, we'll have the first witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the draft has been proceeded in respect of all proceedings for this week. It needs a slight tidying up of text by one word, but that can be dealt with very swiftly. I've been given advance notice by Mr. Kovacic of the nature of his objection in respect of Brix Andersen, and I think that we can accommodate the discussion about those objections under the overall umbrella of a compendious application. I don't think there is a problem. So, yes, may the first witness come in.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: While the witness is coming in, Mr. President, there are two short matters that we would like to raise after the witness has testified. They shouldn't take more than 30 seconds total, at the end of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you'd like to take a seat, Mr. Verhoeven.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I trust that the Chamber has not only --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I trust that the Chamber has not only the summary of Mr. Verhoeven's evidence, but also has or can have provided to it a small bundle of exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Indeed, if one could be left with the witness, that could speed matters. From time to time the witness will need to refer to a map, and although recently we have found maps of some detail and use in particular circumstances, I think probably the witness will be as happy as any with map 2612,2. And if again there is no objection, I'll make mine available, although it has some highlights on it, but the highlights tend to be rather more useful than unhelpful. Mr. Verhoeven, are you a professional soldier in the Belgian army, and have been such since 1976, presently head of either what's called the logistics or the infrastructure department of that army, with the rank of commander, being based in Germany?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: An ECMM monitor from mid-July until October of 1993. Following earlier assignments, did you, after three weeks, become leader of team V1, whose area of concern or responsibility was from Travnik in the north through Guca Gora, Busovaca and Vitez, or the other way around?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you have a notebook which you used for certain purposes in the course of your duties, making, I think, short notes rather than, perhaps, full notes?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: At the time that you made your statement to ICTY investigators, did you have that notebook to hand and did you refer to it for matters of detail?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Has the notebook since then been lost or mislaid?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So that for certain matters of detail not referred to in contemporaneous daily reports, have you had to look at your statement made to investigators, but on the basis that that was itself prepared from earlier contemporaneous notes of your own?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, if you could help me with one thing. Guca Gora. I don't seem to have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can you find this Guca Gora on this map. You'll know how to mark it. What happens, if you leave it on the -- there it is. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: [indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did the Chamber see it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Point to it once more.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And perhaps he could have the pointer, unless its been mislaid.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Just due west of Zenica, northwest of Vitez, northeast by east of Travnik?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Guca Gora, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I am not going to trouble you with this map, Mr. Verhoeven, but have you this morning seen a map which marks out in a bold black line the shape of the pocket under HVO control marked as July 1993?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And although there may be some differences in the details of the perimeter shown on that map, does its general shape --

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: General shape, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: -- accord with your recollection of your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The map to which I am referring is the front-line map that's been provided to the Chamber, or one of them, and it's going to be the subject of evidence later. Mr. Verhoeven, one of the problems, and I've probably already aggravated the problem, is that because we speak in English, we may not make suitable allowance for the interpreters. So I will try and hear when the French translation is finished, and there will be gaps between questions and answers to accommodate that. Did you, on the 31st of July of 1993, meet the defendant Mario Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Do you now have a recollection of where you met him, or are you driven to an assumption about where you met him?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: If my memories are well, I met him in the place where he had his office.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Which was in which town?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: In Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The topic of the discussion and its resolution, please?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: What date did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It's the 31st of July, and this may be a matter for which there isn't a report, but which you will be able to refer to your memory first, because it was covered in your witness statement.

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can you tell us, what was the subject of the exchange? It's not going to be in those documents there, because we don't have a report for it.

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Can I have back the --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The witness statement?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes. Because there are so many dates and so many --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: With the Court's leave, and in the absence of objection, in light of the way the earlier statement was founded on then-contemporaneous documents, may he, so far as necessary, refer to that for assistance?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. As I've said before, it shouldn't be a test of memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It's been highlighted, but it hasn't, I think, been otherwise marked -- sorry, that one has been. I'll take mine out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: At the foot of the first page, meeting of the 31st of July, please.

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What happened on that meeting, please?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: As we did usually, we went to -- as we did usually, we went to -- to see the local commanders and the local authorities. And on that day I met with Mr. Cerkez in Vitez, and we discussed about problems, as we usually did, of exchanges of prisoners, how the prisoners were treated, and those matters. And in that meeting, I was told that three boys were held by the BiH in Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: At that meeting, did Mr. Cerkez want an exchange of visitors on a particular basis?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes, all by all exchanges.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That's all prisoners from one side to be exchanged for all for the other, and he also --

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: -- drew to your attention --

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: -- to these three boys? Very well. I will return to paragraph 4 of the summary at the end of the evidence. We come to the 18th of August, which again is not subject to a report, but is on the second page of your statement, if you need to refer to it. Did you receive information from the imam from Busovaca, or about the imam from Busovaca, that he was not free to move around?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: How did you appear, in a word?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: He was unhappy, and he was frightened.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You were allowed to talk to him in private, but --

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: -- was there any apparent supervision or monitoring of your meetings?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Not directly, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: But indirectly?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: There were HVO soldiers in the neighbourhood. They were looking, but they didn't interfere.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did he explain to you what, in his judgement, was the desire of the Muslim population of Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: They wanted to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Were they allowed to?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Paragraph 6 of the summary: On the 21st of August of 1993 -- and I'll lead unless anybody indicates to me that I shouldn't -- did you pursue a claim by the HVO in Busovaca that Mujahedin fought alongside the BiH, and that they had proof of this, with a foreign soldier?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And you interviewed the person concerned, who appeared to be a Syrian student claiming to have been in Yugoslavia since 1982 and having been mobilised?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's what he told.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: On the 26th of August, did you meet Franjo Kristo, Busovaca's police chief, and did he express himself in strong terms? And, perhaps, turning only to your notes if you need to, tell the Judges what he expressed about Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: He didn't think that it was possible that those two sorts of people, Muslims and Croats, could live together as equal partners.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And in what terms did he describe the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: He said Muslims could eventually live together with the Croats in the new state of -- in Bosnia-Herzegovina, but then as sort of immigrants, just like in other countries, where someone who comes into that country has no right to vote.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. Did he use any terms of abuse about them?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Can you repeat this?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did he use any bad language or bad names about them?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yeah, he called them barbarians or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Paragraph 8: On the 27th of August, did the HVO cut off water supply to the BiH side in Travnik, and did you speak to the HVO president in Travnik about this?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: His explanation was?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: What do you mean by this question?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, what was his reaction to your raising this issue with him? What did he say was the possibility of turning the water back on?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: He couldn't decide that -- he couldn't decide this on his level.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And to what level did he have to refer before he could allow the Muslims in Travnik to have water?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: To Mr. Valenta.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: How did that strike you as a reaction?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: I found it a little bit strange, because it was a local matter, and I knew Mr. Valenta as vice-president. I found it a little bit strange that it had to go until this high level.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. President, one matter of detail: Looking at the statement that was contemporaneously -- or the statement that was taken by the investigators of Commandant Verhoeven, it looks like the water-supply issue that we're talking about deals with Novi Travnik and not Travnik. I wonder if the Prosecution might just clear that up, because I think it's a little unclear.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Would you like to resolve that issue, please, Mr. Verhoeven? Are we talking about Travnik, or Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The first document, not actually covered on the summary, but fits in to the account, is Exhibit 1185,2, for the 28th of August. Is this one of a number of daily reports prepared by you?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Under the heading "Political Situation," and following a meeting with Kresimir Garic, chief of the civilian police in Vitez, do we find an entry halfway down the page where he was expressing the view that -- on the right-hand side of the page -- joint living could be possible in other areas, but not Vitez or Busovaca? Going on to say that joint cooperation or a certain form of cooperation could be possible, but that he was convinced this was a religious war to prevent Muslim domination, and he said he saw the beginning of conflict as caused by Muslim refugees who tried to push the Croats out. And then on the second sheet, over the next page. Were you stopped in Busovaca by an old, desperate Muslim woman who claimed that she had been on four occasions expelled from her home; they last had been living with another Muslim family who now had found a Croat side on the other side to exchange with. And you then make this comment, "that it happens that exchanges of houses through the front lines were being made sometimes with the payment of money to soldiers." And then under assessment, paragraph 8, you make further reference to this by using the word "black," black exchange. Was that something you thought you encountered from time to time, black exchange, exchange for money?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: What I meant with black exchanges -- what I meant, that they were not official.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And sometimes for money?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's what people who were involved, who wanted to pass has told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Paragraph 9 of the summary. The next document in the bundle, 1186,2. Did you on the 30th of August of 1993 meet the military chief of Busovaca, Zarko Milic, who complained of the influx of Croat refugees as a cause of difficulties?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We can see this in the first paragraph of your report. Was there talk there of black exchanges, and did he express concern about increasing criminality caused by the influx of refugees?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Let me turn to the second sheet of this daily report. Can you just deal with what happened at the checkpoint between Vitez and Kruscica. I think you were not allowed to pass without written permission.

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The person operating the checkpoint insisted on your getting permission from whom?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: From Mr. Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Was Colonel Blaskic referred to?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes, but the man at the checkpoint didn't agree with the permission of Mr. Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Which you had? Did you have the permission of Mr. Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Do you mean a written permission?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So it's a question that they would not have been happy with a consent of Blaskic; they required one from Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And if we read on in the entry in your daily report, you were warned that the road to Kruscica was unsafe because they expected an attack on Vitez from that area, and while you were at that checkpoint there was shooting nearby, and there was indeed nervousness in the headquarters, and you noticed the large number of soldiers on the streets of Vitez. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: On the map will you just remind the Chamber where or approximately where this checkpoint was, so that we can just see it. Is the point of your find -- if you leave the map on the ELMO, then we can all see it on the screen. If you use the pointer, that will help. It may be that the map can be a little bit more focused, but it's not the best of maps.

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Here's Kruscica [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Did you also refer directly to Mr. Cerkez that day, as your report suggests?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: How you mean that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, if you read the next part of that paragraph, it begins "Mr. Cerkez told him that." You must interpret that for us.

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: To whom did Mr. Cerkez say this?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: To me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Read the entry to yourself and then explain it to us, if you would be so good.

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: "Mr. Cerkez told me that if BiH should attack, everything, what had happened until now, would have been just a game. HVO was ready to use all their resources, including these which they have not used until now."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. As your first witness statement, built on your then contemporaneous and available notes revealed, and this isn't in the summary, but should be, did you on the 1st of September have a meeting with, amongst other people, your superior, Philip Watkins, and Ambassador Thebault?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Who else was present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Mr. Kordic and a man called Kostroman.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: How long or short was the meeting?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: It was long.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Do you have any present recollection of the detail of what passed in that meeting?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Indeed, has it not been possible for you to see and not been possible for the Prosecution to show you any document that deals with that meeting?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Apart from this occasion, did you see Kordic on any other occasions, or try to see him?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, did you hear things about him and about the personalities in the Lasva Valley during your tour of operation?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you have any clear understanding of any separation of civilian and military authority?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Do you mean in general?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In general, and so far as individuals are concerned in particular.

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes. We tried to locate the functions of the different authorities we met.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Was it ever possible to do that with precision?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: This was not always possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'll return to this paragraph for further comment at the end of your evidence. But just before I do move on, did you see Valenta once or more than once?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: I saw him more than once.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Were you able to make any comparison between the appearances or trappings of authority or power associated with Valenta, on the one hand, and with Kordic on the other?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Not really proof, just it was -- it was for me easier to go to get to Valenta as to Mr. Kordic. Mr. Kordic was -- I had the feeling on a higher level as Mr. Valenta.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Because?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Because it was on my level easier to go to Mr. Valenta, that's one; and second, I had the impression that Mr. Kordic was better surrounded, more protected.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: By what sort of procedures or what sort of people?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: By soldiers, bodyguards.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. Paragraph 11. On the 3rd of September did you learn that the three Croat boys, whom you mentioned earlier, had been exchanged for three sick Muslim prisoners who had been held by the HVO in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Now, those three Croat boys had been held by the BiH. Did you see them in captivity?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes, I visit them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What did their conditions of detention appear to be?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Normal, as far as boys who are kept in captivity can be. But they were not maltreated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The 8th of September next. Reference to the map, if necessary. Remind the Chamber of the area. Was there an attack in the area of the region of Stari Bila on the 8th of September?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And was there a strategic significance in that area, and was the attack successful in pushing the BiH line back to a degree, but can you now -- if that be correct, can you explain it on the map, please.

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes. I'll put it back. This is the Bila feature [indicates]. The front line at this moment were very narrow to the road, and it was for Croat, HVO people, very dangerous to use the road because of sniper activities by BiH. After the attack, the road was clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. Give me a minute. There is a paperwork problem. Now, I have raced ahead of the paperwork. My mistake entirely. But can we just correct things by going back to the documents that should be before you. The next one in the pile should be 1187,1, and it is -- and that's daily report for the 31st of August, the second sheet of which requires just very brief consideration, where I should have asked you to deal with the full paragraph that deals with your being stopped at the HVO checkpoint between Vitez and Kruscica, not being allowed to pass. And at the end of the same paragraph you say that, "It's likely that the HVO doesn't want any NGO or ECMM to pass, because of supplies delivered to Kruscica without result in the water and the prisoner's case." Does that mean without resolution of the problem of the water and prisoner case?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And this was more or less confirmed by the liaison officer of the HVO, who stated that the command of the operational zone, Blaskic, had some problems with the responsible brigade commander, Mr. Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. If we turn to the next document in the bundle, it should be 1195,2, for the 4th of September. And although it's not touched on in the summary, I think you draw to our attention on the second sheet, again, in the first complete paragraph, the position on the checkpoints between Zenica and the Busovaca junction, where the situation was getting worse, where people were having to wait for days, or some days. And you say this: "The problem should be that the BiH want some important people out of Busovaca, which the HVO refuses. They were prepared to let unimportant Muslims pass without problems." Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We turn to the 8th of September, the supporting document is now a milinfosum which is numbered Z1196. Halfway down the entry for Vitez, on the first sheet, you may find what supports your evidence, but was there an attack on the 8th of September by the HVO in the region of Stari Bila?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: An area previously held, strategic, overlooking the road, and then that was what was pushed back?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. So we can turn to the 9th of September, which is now dependent on your -- not dependent on, but refers to your daily report. Did you have a meeting on the 9th of September, Document 1198,2, with Zoran Maric, the mayor of Busovaca, he again talking of civilians on the road from Zenica to Busovaca, and black exchange that took place in that area, he complaining that those exchanges were illegal and should be stopped? And at the foot of the first page of this document, we see he said that the civilian police of Busovaca had received order to stop Croats at the checkpoint and protect [sic] them coming to Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And you saw some 60 people waiting to go to Busovaca, I think?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Perhaps interesting to note, over the page, as your assessment in relation to the Bila feature of which you have already told us -- perhaps not the Bila feature, but the high ground which dominates the BiH-held area of responsibility of Sadovace, Bukve, and Brdo -- that they can't allow a threat and will be forced to gain back to the Bila feature, but you hope not?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: I said I hope I am not in BritBat -- in BritBat at that moment, because I was there at the first attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The 20th of September -- I beg your pardon; before we come to that, we must look briefly at the daily report for the 12th of September, which is not covered in the summary, but there's something I think you want to draw to our attention there. That's Document 1199,1. We can see -- do you have that one there? It may be because I've got two copies. Here's one coming your way.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I trust the Chamber has Z1199,1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We see, under "Political Situation," your account that there were no more than 40 Muslims left in Busovaca because they went to Zenica by the unofficial exchanges which you had been reporting on over the previous weeks?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: If I could just register a brief objection to the phraseology of that question, Your Honour: It appears that this report is summarising a conclusion that someone else has said, rather than what the witness has said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can you deal with that, please, Mr. Verhoeven?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes, I was told that there are no more than 40 Muslims --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, you were told, but --

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: -- left in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: -- first of all, by whom were you told?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: By the imam.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In your experience, what measure of contact did he have with Muslim occupants of Busovaca, and how reliable was he up and until then as a narrator, as a provider of information?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: He was allowed to get visits from other Muslims at his home.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: How reliable or unreliable had you found him to be, if you had been able to assess his reliability?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: I think he spoke the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. In the middle of the same page, you make reference to the number of people at Checkpoint Olimpik decreasing. You saw more Muslims on the other side waiting to pass. If you can remember, and by reference to the map, and using the pointer, tell us about where Checkpoint Olimpik was. If you can't recall at this remove of time --

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well. Paragraph 14, 10th of September, the daily report Z1207,1: Did you on that day have a meeting, as we can see, with Darko Gelic, the HVO liaison officer for Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What was said by way of threat or promise about the explosive factory?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: HVO would not allow BiH to get to the explosive factory; they rather would blow them -- blow him up.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Was there an identifiable risk to civilians in blowing it up?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Was that risk drawn to their attention?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: They said the Croat people would fight until the end and would take their destiny, accept their destiny.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document is the daily report for the 21st of September, Z1210,1, and again, under your assessment, the same point is dealt with: They have decided to blow up the explosive factory in Vitez if the BiH continue with their aim of taking the factory. Both parties are aware of the consequences. It seems that the military advantage of holding it is the crucial factor.

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: 22nd of September, paragraph 15, document Z1211,1: Did you on this day, the 22nd of September, meet Valenta, discuss the Geneva maps, and did he assert that there was no Croat municipality which had a Muslim majority, although there were many Muslim municipalities in which there was a Croat majority?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And he said, after dealing with access to the sea, he explained that the water and electricity problems were easily solvable, but he claimed the Muslims did not want to cooperate, and so he was prepared to do the same thing?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And then, over the page, we can see he emphasised the humanitarian difficulties facing the Croats in the coming winter.

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If we then go to the next document, the 23rd of September, although it's not in the summary, just one point you want to draw to our attention on what is document Z1212,1. Where under your assessment you say that the battle of Vitez has reached its top and will go on for a few days, and that if the water and electricity problems for Novi Travnik and Novi Bila is not solved, the HVO will execute its threat and cut water and electricity for Zenica and Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Paragraph 16 of the summary, the 27th of October, document 1217,1. Did you again meet Zoran Maric, as the first paragraph of your daily report reveals?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you ask him in particular about the burning of a mosque?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: About the burning of a mosque.

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It's in the first paragraph. Did you ask him about that?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Let me just register one objection to the relevance of this line of questioning, Mr. President. The burning of the mosque in September of 1993 is not an item charged in the parts of the indictment addressed to the damage and destruction of religious institutions. So we don't believe that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Because it's not in the indictment, doesn't mean it's not within the parameters of what's relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think you asked him if he met the imam to discuss the situation of the Muslims, and he said he'd do this after an investigation into the burning of the mosque. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your comment, arising from this, was that in reality the imam is considered more a hostage than a conversation partner. Is there anything you want to add to the comment in explanation of that?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Well, the Major didn't speak with the imam. When I asked him, he denied it. He didn't want to go to the imam, and the imam was not able to move. So for me and my comment, I meant that he was hold there, perhaps for later exchange against the Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And, as a matter of fact, did you ever get a report on the burning of the mosque?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Paragraph 17 of the summary. Did you on that day or about that day, the 27th of September, receive a letter from Blaskic dealing with planned prisoner exchange of persons from Travnik held by the BiH against Muslims held by the HVO, Stari Vitez for Vitez?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: On the 1st of October did you learn that the new chief of the civilian police in Busovaca was Drago Ljubos? Don't worry about the documents. This comes from your statement, so it came from your notebook.

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: On the 2nd of October did you with two ECMM cars go to Vitez to pick up a family that was supposed to be exchanged, having been subject to an agreement with Blaskic some days before?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Briefly, what happened so far as some HVO soldiers in uniform were concerned?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: They started shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What sort of uniform were they in?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Black uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you leave the area and go to Blaskic to complain?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Who else was present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Mr. Gelic, the HVO liaison officer, Mr. Blaskic, Mr. Cerkez, and some military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If we turn to the next document, it may be the next document, but one in the bundle, it will be 1229. Is this a special report of that incident prepared by you?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We've already summarised the effect of it. And going through things chronologically, but with an eye to that document, on the 4th of October did Ljubos, the new police chief, receive a visit from you; he maintaining that he was doing all he could to protect the Muslim population, and giving an explanation for the burning of the mosque?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What was that explanation?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: He said that most likely the mosque was being hit by a shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you check that out?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: By visiting the area?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Were you able to find any evidence to support the suggestion that the mosque had been hit by a shell?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: No. I have seen no sign of damage from a shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: On the 5th of October, did you visit Zoran Maric again? This comes from your notes as set out in your first statement.

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did he speak of presence at the second session of the government, as it was described, of Herceg-Bosnia in Neum?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes. He told me he just came back from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did he say anything about the purpose of that government session, if government it was?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Can you explain your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. Did he say what was discussed at the session in Neum? And it may be you'll want to look to your --

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: One moment. They discussed several matters. They discussed the creation of the republic; they discussed problems of human rights and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did he say anything --

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That is what he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did he say anything about his ability or inability to help the Muslims in Busovaca or anything about linkage of their problems with other problems?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: No. Those problems were linked with other problems, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Which ones did he say the position of the Busovaca Muslims were linked to? Can you recall?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. The problem of the Muslims in Busovaca was linked with the problems of the Croats in Travnik and Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Next document, the last of its type, is Z1235 dated October the 6th. A letter from Colonel Blaskic, responding to your letter of the 2nd of October, which dealt with what had happened to you. It expresses in the first paragraph dismay and shock. In the second paragraph it says he started an investigation, and said that the act of violence had been done by Slaven Kraljevic and Goran Medjugorac, to try and stop her leaving Vitez, in reference to a love affair and reference to drink. Saying he was -- he, Blaskic, was responsible for the violence done, although it came as a result of an emotional state, and saying that the matter had been handed over to a military court. Did you hear any more about that inquiry after that?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Paragraph 22 of the summary. Helicopters. What, if anything, did you hear or see of helicopters?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: I heard talking about helicopters and one time I have seen one. It was a transporter helicopter.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Could you decide for which side it was working?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: I think while it was in HVO territory, that it was HVO helicopter.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did it have markings associating it with any particular party?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: At the time you were in the area, we've heard already of one participant going to meetings of the parliament at Neum. Were you aware of others going there?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes. I think Mr. Valenta was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Would it have been possible for Mr. Valenta or the other man to reach these parliamentary sessions by road?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: I don't think so, because of the checkpoints on the front lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And of course, just to remind the judges, the drawing that you've said that described the position that you saw is a contained envelope around Vitez and Busovaca, and stops short of Kiseljak and Neum?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Finally, back to paragraph 4 of the summary, as I said I would. The one outstanding document in the list, your handwritten list, Z1218. Described in paragraph 4 as a contemporaneous listing. In fact, you prepared this document when?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: The document, I handed it over to the man who was after me, to make for him his work a little bit easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And we see under Busovaca the first name is the name Dario Kordic, vice-president of the republic of Herceg-Bosnia. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We see in the last name on this part of the list, you needn't read the name out, but we can see the name of the imam, and in brackets you've put the word?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: "Kept."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Meaning?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: He was under -- he should stay at home in his house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: After Kacuni you deal with Vitez. Valenta first, vice-president of the republic; and then Blaskic and other names?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Then over the page, the commander of the Viteska Brigade, Dario Kordic. Thank you very much. Please wait there, you may be asked further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And good morning, Mr. Verhoeven. My name is Steven Sayers and I represent Dario Kordic. Just one initial question. If you take a look at the transcript, the commander of the Viteska Brigade is identified as Dario Kordic on page 35, line 14. Just take a look at the TV screen. Did you mean to say Mario Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: You mean -- I don't get your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's a mistake, Mr. Sayers. We needn't waste any time with it. We can see from the document that the name should be Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I think that's correct, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just a few questions for you, commandant. I take it that you have been a professional soldier for the last 23 years?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: With the Belgian army, correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You were in Central Bosnia performing functions as an European community monitor mission monitor from July the 25th of 1993, correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: From July to October, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And I believe that you left on October the 12th of 1993?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: It's possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: So it would be fair to say that you were in the area for three months. And that three-month tour that you spent in Central Bosnia was a standard length of time for monitors basically to spend in their tours with the European Community Monitoring Mission, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: At that moment it wasn't. I spent a little more time as normally, because I was -- at the first time I was reserve. Someone had to be replaced, so I went earlier as normally was planned. It was at that moment, I think, nine weeks or something for one normal tour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. So you are saying that the normal length of time for a monitor to spend in Central Bosnia at this time was nine weeks?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: About that, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That's fine. Now, commandant, you do not speak Croatian yourself, do you?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Accordingly, obviously, you had to use interpreters in order to be able to conduct conversations with the people about whom you've testified today; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Commandant, as you prepared to take up your duties in Central Bosnia, you first travelled I believe to Zagreb, the capital of Croatia; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And I believe that you received a briefing on the situation that you would likely encounter in Central Bosnia at that time?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: How long did the briefing last, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Two days, two or three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: How much of the briefing was devoted to Central Bosnia, as opposed to the Balkans generally?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: There was not so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you, yourself, actually do any reading or undertake any additional studies to help you understand the historical, ethnic, military, and political situation that you would encounter when you actually arrived in Central Bosnia, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: I -- I did not have the time to make some special analyses or studies, if that is what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And who actually gave you the briefing, sir, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: It was the operational officer in Zagreb, and then, of course, the ambassador, and the operational officer in Zenica, and my superior, Mr. Watkins.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Would you agree that the ECMM at this time in 1993, during your tour of duty, was manned principally by military officers who had been assembled from various European and other nations, and they were assigned to perform as monitors for the nine weeks that you've just identified?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: As I understand it, sir, the headquarters of the ECMM was in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And just so that it's clear, I believe that there are separate regional headquarters, if you like, called regional centres, one of which was in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And were you actually based in Zenica, primarily, as you travelled around Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that the city of Zenica, while you were there, was a city of some -- what, 150.000; something in that area?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's possible. It's a big city.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And there's no question that the city was exclusively under the control of Muslim political and military forces at the time that you were there; would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In fact, sir, I believe that there were no military units from the HVO located in Zenica when you arrived on the ground on July the 25th of 1993?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you understand that the HVO military units in Zenica had actually been defeated in the April 1993 fighting, just a few months before you arrived?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: You mean if I knew it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes. Did you understand that that was the case? Or don't you know?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That's fine. Within the regional centre organisations, sir, of the ECMM, would it also be fair to say that there were various coordination centres that reported to the regional centres as well?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And in the Zenica area, the principal coordination centre, if you like, that coordinated your activities, would have been located in Travnik at all times; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: The CC, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is that a convenient moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We'll adjourn for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sayers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Commandant, as we were examining the structure of the ECMM, we had talked about regional centres and coordination centres, and I believe on the ground, at the most fundamental level, you had a number of teams of two monitors with a driver and an interpreter, and they in turn prepared daily reports that were submitted to the coordination centre; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And then the coordination centre presumably, sir, sent the reports or collated the reports, prepared summaries, and sent them to the regional centre in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In Zenica the same process occurred; summaries of those reports were prepared and submitted up the line to the headquarters in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. And you were one of the monitors on Team V2, was it?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Victor 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Victor 1. The usual practice was to have an incoming monitor basically taken around and introduced to people by someone who had actually performed as a monitor for some period of time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And who was the monitor who introduced you around, Commandant?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: This was a Norwegian. The first name was Stefan. I don't remember the last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Very well. Now, your duties as a monitor consisted principally of speaking with people on both sides of the conflict to obtain information on the military, civilian, and humanitarian front; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And also to respond to any particular requests for information that you received from either the regional centre or the coordination centre; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, after being in Central Bosnia for three weeks, you were deemed to be sufficiently knowledgeable and experienced to head up your own monitor team, V1; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And I believe that you worked with a Greek army officer by the name of Mr. Bekos?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Would you agree that one of the principal problems that confronted you as a monitor was the huge number of refugees that had come into Central Bosnia who had been forced out of their homes during the civil war in 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And, in fact, I believe, sir, that you saw one good example of the sheer magnitude of this problem in the town of Busovaca itself, as you've previously described?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You talked about a meeting that you had on August the 30th with the chief of military police, Mr. Zarko Milic, in Busovaca, and you were shown an exhibit -- I believe it was a daily report that you had prepared yourself -- which was marked as Exhibit Z1186,2. Now, Mr. Milic did tell you that he was the chief of military police in that town; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do you recall the identity of the chief of military police in Vitez, sir? Was that Pasko Ljubicic?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't remember the names. I -- I should look at my list.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It's true that the chief of military police in Busovaca, the Mr. Milic that you've identified, informed you that the huge influx of refugees into the town were causing a large number of problems; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: He emphasised to you that the task of the military police was to try to protect the remaining Muslim citizens in Busovaca; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: But that this was difficult to do because of the large number of displaced, dispossessed, angry Croat refugees; right?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You saw that yourself in the town?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: He also emphasised to you that this was the general policy of the HVO, to try to protect the Muslim minority in Busovaca; right?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And I believe he actually showed you a written order from his commander, Colonel Blaskic, which actually ordered this policy to be put into force in Busovaca; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: He showed me a written order, but I -- I can't remember if the order was signed, by whom the order was signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. There is no question, though, sir, that the military police came under the authority, the jurisdiction of the Central Bosnia operative zone commander Colonel Blaskic, is there?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: As I saw there, [Realtime transcript read in error "as a soldier"] it would be normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Right. Just a few questions, sir, on the --

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: I didn't say "as I saw there." I said "as a soldier." I could mean that it was so, that the military police comes under --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Right. You were saying that the transcript says "as I saw there," and really what you were saying was "as a soldier," and you were describing the normal chain of command?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Let me ask you a few questions, commandant, on the subject of the so-called black exchanges that you talked about. These so-called black exchanges involved unofficial or illegal attempts of civilians on both sides to cross the front lines, Muslims from Croat controlled areas into Muslim controlled areas, and Croats from Muslim --

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Muslim controlled area to Croat --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Right. Let me just make sure that I got it correct on the record. Muslims from Croat controlled areas, trying to get into Muslim controlled areas, and Croats from Muslim controlled areas trying it get into Croat controlled areas; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And it's true that your information was that these elicit exchanges were strictly forbidden by the authorities on both sides, both the Muslim authorities and the HVO authorities; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's what they said, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: But these exchanges were going on nonetheless through a variety of means, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In fact, sir, in one of these occasions on September the 4th you noted in your statement that Muslim authorities were refusing to let civilians across the front lines, Croat civilians that is, to pass into HVO controlled territory; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Did you say the 3rd of September?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The 4th of September, I believe it was. It's on page 5 of your statement, actually. And you say that you saw civilians on the road between Zenica and Busovaca, the situation was getting worse.

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Some had been there for as long as three days and they couldn't return to their homes because other people had taken them over already.

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: But despite that, they were still not allowed by the Muslim forces to leave Muslim controlled territory; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You made some reference during your testimony to the water supply problems in Novi Travnik. It's true that both sides were using utility interruptions, utility such as water and electricity, as one of their tools during this war; isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: There was one incident, it's on August the 22nd, I believe, following a meeting that you had had with Mr. Darko Gelic, in which he complained that the Red Cross was illegally moving three persons from Stari Vitez without prior clearance from the HVO authorities. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And these people, these three sick Muslims from Stari Vitez, were actually part of a Red Cross contingent that was stopped at a HVO checkpoint, and then the ill Muslims were taken to the field hospital in Vitez for treatment; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's what he said, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And it was these sick people that were eventually exchanged for the three young boys that you've talked about, I take it?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, you had, and I think you've related this to the Court, sir, several meetings with representatives of the civilian government in Busovaca, most notably with Mr. Zoran Maric, throughout your tour; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you find it was easy to gain access to Mr. Maric to discuss local issues or problems that you wanted to discuss with him?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: What do you mean with easy?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: If the question is unclear, that's my fault, not yours. Did you ever encounter any problems in gaining access to see Mr. Maric?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: I received no problems, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And you discussed a number of issues with him such as, for example, the black exchanges about which we've talked, and Mr. Maric confirmed to you that the civilian exchanges were completely illegal; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: He told you that he, in fact, had ordered them stopped, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And one of the problems caused by these incoming Croat refugees and one of the reasons that he'd ordered this practice stopped was because Croat refugees who came into Busovaca were trying to push Muslims living in that town out of their houses; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's what he said, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And he told you that the Busovaca police authorities had received orders to stop Croat civilians at checkpoints in order to prevent them from coming into Busovaca, didn't he, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And wouldn't you agree that this problem of civilians wanting to pass from territory controlled by one ethnic group into another was an extremely delicate problem in view of all the allegations of ethnic cleansing that were flying around in Central Bosnia in 1993?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes, it's a very delicate problem. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You made a reference, sir, to the fact that Mr. Maric and you had a meeting, I believe it was on October the 5th of 1993, following Mr. Maric's return from a session of the government of the republic of -- the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosnia in Neum. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you've got the document, perhaps you could refer to it for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I think it appears, commandant, on page 8, the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes. He said to me he had just returned from Neum.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. And did you understand that he was a delegate in the House of Representatives of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: I didn't know his right function, but while he was there, I mean, he had something to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say, commandant, that you never had the opportunity to discuss Mr. Maric's function within the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosnia with him at any time?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Now, it's also true that you had many meetings with Mr. Valenta in Vitez during the three months of your tour of duty; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That depends on what you mean with "many." A few. I had a few.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Was it your understanding, sir, that he was a vice-president of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he said and that's how he was known at the ECMM level.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do you know how many other vice-presidents of that organisation there were in 1993, and who they were?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: I have knowledge of two, Mr. Valenta and Mr. Kordic. I don't know if there were more.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Let me suggest to you, sir, that Mr. Kordic was not, in fact, ever a vice-president of the HVO; he was actually a vice-president of a body called the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: He was -- I just put in the information I had. You could say it's not that way, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you ever receive information, sir, that the President of the HVO was actually Dr. Jadranko Prlic?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: The name doesn't mean anything to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you know that Mr. Valenta, sir, was actually a representative of the Croat side at the talks held in Geneva in the summer of 1993 that immediately preceded the formulation of the Stoltenberg-Owen plan?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: I don't know if he was in Geneva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: If I suggested to you that Mr. Valenta was actually the representative of the Croat side for Central Bosnia, would that jog your memory, or does that not have a familiar ring to it at all to you?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: I -- I know, and I knew, that Mr. Valenta had a superior function for the Croats in Central Bosnia. But his -- how far his power was, I can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Commandant, I don't want to put you on the spot, but would it be fair to say that you really did not know what functions Mr. Valenta actually had within the political institutions of the Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina generally and in Central Bosnia specifically?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: If you mean a precise job description, I can't give, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And the same is true with Mr. Kordic, whom you met only once throughout your tour, I take it?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In fact, you have no recollection of that meeting with Mr. Kordic on September the 1st at all?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness said that, so there is --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Very well, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- no need to repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You made a reference in your statements to the fact that your immediate superior, Philip Watkins, actually prepared a special report on the results of that meeting on September the 1st, 1993. Have you ever seen a copy of that special report?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just a few final questions on Mr. Valenta. You actually had a discussion with him relating to ongoing talks in Geneva and the issue of maps and so forth, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And he told you that he was prepared to begin peace negotiations with the Muslim side and to resolve issues such as the interruption of water and power supplies, but that he was prepared only to initiate those discussions at a high level; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And I don't mean to trap you, sir. I think you recorded that on your statement at page 6, under the chronological entry for September the 22nd; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. And you've already stated that you summarised your discussions with him in your daily report of that date, and that's already been made an exhibit, so that doesn't need to detain us. Throughout your tour, sir, there isn't any doubt that Colonel Blaskic was, in fact, the operational zone commander of all HVO armed forces in the Vitez/Busovaca pocket, is there?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's how he was known at the ECMM, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: But I believe, sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I believe, sir, that you only, yourself, met Colonel Blaskic a total of three times during your tour in Central Bosnia, and that your principal dealings were with his liaison officer?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, Vitez, would it be fair to say, was a fairly dangerous place to find yourself or to be walking around in the summer of 1993, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In one of your meetings with Mr. Gelic -- I believe it was on August the 18th, 1993, one of your first meetings -- he told you that one of the tactics that the Muslim forces were using was to be wearing HVO uniforms during an attack; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's what he told, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And that in a subsequent meeting with him, on September the 23rd, he gave you an update on the military situation, and as you were talking, three shells landed just a few metres away from you; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: A few questions in connection, sir, with the SPS or Vitezit factory, the explosives factory that was located just to the northwest of Vitez. There is no question that that was an important strategic objective for both sides, for the HVO to retain control of it and for the Muslim forces to capture the factory; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In fact, you record in your August the 31st, 1993, report, Z1187,1, that it is clear to you that the ABiH is looking hungrily towards the explosives factory, and they demonstrated that attitude throughout your tour in Central Bosnia; isn't that true, Commandant?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And to prevent that, Mr. Gelic told you that the Croat side would be prepared to explode the 100 tonnes of ammunition and explosives that were contained in the factory, if necessary; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: A fairly desperate move, I think you'll agree, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: But that never actually occurred, did it?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Not when I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: One other question about shelling, sir: I believe that you were present at the Nova Bila hospital on September the 11th of 1993, just one day after it had been shelled by 120-millimetre rounds, one of which only landed two metres away from the hospital; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And that explosion basically blew out all of the windows and resulted in several casualties, people inside the hospital; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHAN VERHOEVEN
utterances.text: I was told that there had been casualties, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
